claim: At the HYMN unit the same question resolves, and the sign flips with scope. Over all 1,028 hymns, Spearman rho between book number and the hymn's Arnold-late pada share is +0.2125 (permutation p = 0.0002, 5,000 shuffles). Over books 1-9 alone it is -0.1526 (p = 0.0002). Over the family books 2-7 alone it is +0.1648 (p = 0.0012).
notes: THREE CAVEATS, none optional. It is still Arnold's instrument, so it inherits everything A-1 records. Hymns within a book are not independent observations, so the permutation p is optimistic. And the distribution is severely zero-inflated - 65.4% of all hymns, and 74.9% of hymns in books 1-9, contain no late pada at all, and the median late share is 0.000 in every book but 10 - so the all-books result is driven substantially by book 10 and by heavy ties. This row is therefore NOT a finding about the Rigveda. What it establishes is that the question is answerable at a finer unit, that the answer is scope-dependent, and that within the family books the sign runs TOWARD the standard ordering rather than away from it. Added 2026-09-09 after adversarial re-review pointed out that A-2's own falsifier named this test and the unit had not run it: BF-031.
